english: Let $L_1:\ \dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{1}=\dfrac{z-4}{1}$ and $L_2:\ \dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y-\mu}{-1}=\dfrac{z}{2}$, where $\mu$ is a real number such that $L_1$ and $L_2$ are skew lines and the line of shortest distance between $L_1$ and $L_2$ intersects the $z$-axis. Let $d$ be the shortest distance between $L_1$ and $L_2$ for this value of $\mu$. Then the value of $\mu-d^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $L_1:\ \dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{1}=\dfrac{z-4}{1}$ तथा $L_2:\ \dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y-\mu}{-1}=\dfrac{z}{2}$ हैं, जहाँ $\mu$ एक ऐसी वास्तविक संख्या है कि $L_1$ तथा $L_2$ विषमतलीय रेखाएँ हैं तथा $L_1$ और $L_2$ के बीच की न्यूनतम दूरी की रेखा $z$-अक्ष को प्रतिच्छेद करती है। माना कि $\mu$ के इस मान के लिए $L_1$ तथा $L_2$ के बीच की न्यूनतम दूरी $d$ है। तब $\mu-d^{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Twice the first minus the second: $-9s+3\mu-3=0$, so $s=\dfrac{\mu-1}{3}$; then $3t=6s-\mu+4=\mu+2$, so $t=\dfrac{\mu+2}{3}$.
Hence $P=\left(\dfrac{2\mu+1}{3},\dfrac{\mu+5}{3},\dfrac{\mu+11}{3}\right)$, and the line of shortest distance has direction $(2,1,1)\times(1,-1,2)=(3,-3,-3)$, that is $(1,-1,-1)$.
The $z$-axis passes through $O$ with direction $(0,0,1)$. It is not parallel to $(1,-1,-1)$, so the two lines intersect if and only if they are coplanar:
For $\mu=-2$: $s=-1$, $t=0$, $P(-1,1,3)$, $Q(2,-2,0)$, and $\overrightarrow{PQ}=(3,-3,-3)$, so $d=3\sqrt3\neq0$ and the lines are indeed skew. (The line $PQ$ meets the $z$-axis at $(0,0,2)$.)
originality_note: New: the line L2 slides with a parameter, and the parameter is fixed by asking that the common perpendicular cut the z-axis, a coplanarity condition on a line that itself depends on mu (way 3, a family with a second condition). Closest known: shortest distance between given skew lines; lines meeting the coordinate axes. Different because: the condition is imposed on the line of shortest distance, so its feet must be found as functions of mu before the determinant is used.
blueprint_concepts: Shortest Distance Line Equation: Finding the symmetrical equation of the line of shortest distance between skew lines.

concept_use.Shortest distance between two lines: d^2 = PQ^2 = 27 at mu = -2 (checked by |AB.(u x v)|/|u x v| = 3 sqrt3), and d != 0 confirms the lines are skew.
concept_use.Shortest Distance Line Equation: Finding: Feet P, Q as functions of mu from PQ perpendicular to both lines, giving the common perpendicular through P((2mu+1)/3, (mu+5)/3, (mu+11)/3) with direction (1,-1,-1).
concept_use.Coplanarity of two lines (determinant co: The common perpendicular meets the z-axis iff the determinant of OP, k, (1,-1,-1) vanishes: x_P + y_P = 0, so mu = -2.

justification: Two ideas linked: parametric feet of the common perpendicular with a free parameter, and the coplanarity determinant applied to that perpendicular; then the distance. Comparable to the line-family question 2023-P1-Q16 (L3).
